title: To Thy Cross and Resurrection
description: To Thy Cross and Resurrection in Tonic Solfa to ST. OSWALD, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the East (Paisley, in print by 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to ST. OSWALD; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: To Thy Cross and Re-sur-rec-tion, Laud and praise we hum-bly give; In Thy death and life im-mor-tal, We will die, and ev-er live.

lines: Laud and praise we humbly give;
In Thy death and life immortal,
We will die, and ever live.
Thou to God hast brought me nigh;
Christ the humble! by Thy meekness,
Thou hast raised my horn on high.
Source of life! O Christ, the anguish
Lifts me to the bliss abiding,
Where from suffering, souls are free.
Christ, to Thee be ever given,
By the souls in sorrow singing,
By the souls redeemed in heaven.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the East (by 1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the East; set to ST. OSWALD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
